xmldoc.short_description: Determine approximate equality of whole arrays with a norm.

param_input_item.param_description: numeric arrays (double, single, integer, real or complex, full or sparse).
relative precision: nonnegative finite real numeric scalar, 0 by default.

param_output_item.param_description: logical scalar: true when A and B are approximately equal as whole arrays.

description.p: TF = isapproxnorm(A, B, precision) compares A and B as whole arrays and returns a single logical value.
A and B are approximately equal when norm(A - B, 'fro') <= precision * min(norm(A, 'fro'), norm(B, 'fro')).
Real and imaginary parts are checked separately. NaN, Inf and -Inf values must be at the same places in A and B, and are then left out of the norms.
A large element can absorb a small error on other elements, unlike the element-wise comparison of isapprox.
A and B must have the same dimensions, otherwise the result is false. Two empty arrays are equal when their dimensions are equal.
When A or B is sparse, both arrays must have the same pattern of nonzero values.
Values are converted to double precision before the comparison, and very large values are scaled so that the norms do not overflow. With a precision of 0, A and B must be equal.
assert_isapprox uses isapproxnorm for its relative comparison.

example_item.example_item_data: isapproxnorm([1 NaN Inf], [1 NaN Inf], eps) isapproxnorm([NaN 1], [1 NaN], eps)

history_item.history_description: initial version, takes over the whole-array comparison of the previous isapprox.
